items.summary: The Tech Policy Press newsletter of Oct. 25, 2026 opens with remarks from a Montreal conference on Attention: Democracy Rebuilt, hosted by Paradigms, McGill University, the Max Bell School of Public Policy and the Centre for Media, Technology and Democracy. Maria Ressa argued that strongmen and tech oligarchs reinforce each other's power. The newsletter then surveys news across Brazil, Europe, India and beyond, covering Meta's 48-hour deadline over content moderation in Brazil, AI-generated election misinformation ahead of US midterms, spyware targeting EU officials, a proposed 30% cut to civil society funding, protests against the Google-Adani data center campus near Visakhapatnam, and Freedom on the Net reporting internet freedom declined for the 16th consecutive year. Contributors include Daniel Arnaudo, Laís Martins, Mark Scott, Vaishnavi Patil, Barry Lynn and Mihir Kshirsagar.
items.title: Tech Policy Press newsletter surveys democracy, surveillance and AI policy

items.summary: On World Stroke Day (Oct 29), Andrew Choong, a vascular surgeon, warns people not to dismiss symptoms that vanish. A transient ischaemic attack shows the same signs as a stroke but resolves within minutes, yet signals a clot has reached the brain and may return. The stroke risk peaks in the first days or weeks. An Oxford study published in The Lancet found patients assessed and treated within a day had an 80% lower chance of a stroke over three months than those seen through routine appointments; speed matters most. He advises going to an emergency department the same day, even if feeling well.
items.title: Surgeon urges fast action on mini-strokes ahead of World Stroke Day

items.summary: Josephine Lim Teo Hwee argues that Singapore's progress in digitalisation should prompt a review of the requirement for physical signatures on deeds. She notes electronic platforms can provide identity verification, timestamps and audit trails, while wet-ink signing creates costs and inconvenience especially for overseas or elderly parties. Calling on ministries and regulators to consult legal practitioners and the public, she suggests a risk-based framework that permits secure electronic execution where risks are managed.
items.title: Singapore writer questions physical signature rules for deeds

items.summary: Apollo Global Management chief economist Torsten Slok reports in a recent note that, outside the tech industry, profit margins and revenue per worker appear flat among S&P 500 companies minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla. Slok says AI has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America beyond tech, arguing it converts cheap intelligence into judgment rather than growth.
items.title: Apollo economist says AI yields no financial payoff for most firms

items.summary: Researchers at Forever Security discovered a tactic in which a malicious AGENTS.md markdown file placed in a customer's ~/Downloads folder tricked an AI coding agent into installing the rogue npm package 'function-color.' They reproduced it against OpenAI Codex and demonstrated that Claude Code could leak OAuth tokens via a similar CLAUDE.md technique. The researchers told BleepingComputer there is nothing for OpenAI or Anthropic to patch, since agents follow these files by design; they attribute initial file placement to web pages writing into the Downloads folder without user interaction. Forever researcher Gal Weizman said hundreds of customers run such agents from ~/Downloads, with Claude Code alone launching more than 1,300 sessions there.
items.title: Forever Security researchers show how an AGENTS.md file can hijack AI coding agents

items.summary: Electrek reports that for a second straight year the highest-rated lawnmowers on Amazon burn no gas, attributing the shift to rising fuel prices and tightening noise and small-engine-emissions rules. The list ranks products with at least 2,000 reviews averaging four stars or higher; among them were battery-electric units from EGO Power, Greenworks and Worx. Top picks include the EGO POWER+ LM2112 push mower rated 4.5 stars across more than 2,200 Amazon reviews, and a Greenworks 40V 16-inch model with an impressive 4.2-star rating after more than 12,000 verified reviews. The article notes electric mowers are quieter, safer and do not emit exhaust while walking behind them, though it also points readers toward rebates from state clean-air regulators and solar installers like EnergySage for broader adoption.
items.title: Amazon's top-rated mowers are electric, per Electrek

items.summary: Alex Gibney's documentary "Musk" was set to open on October 16 across roughly 472 screens, but distributor Bleecker Street withdrew it after just one week. Film industry press reported that Outerlight had acquired Bleecker Street from eBay founder Pierre Omidyar; the new owner also backs Passionflix, a streaming service run by Elon Musk's sister Tosca. HR reporter Mia Galuppo noted this ironic connection while reporting on the sale and an optimistic expansion of the film's release just days before it was pulled.
items.title: Bleecker Street Pulls Alex Gibney's Elon Musk Documentary After One Week

items.summary: Family-owned Wickham Freight Lines took delivery of the Sunswap Endurance, billed as Australia’s first regular-production solar-powered battery-electric trailer refrigeration unit. After a trial run from Sydney to Brisbane and back—1,670 km over more than 30 hours—the drivers returned with over 65% of battery capacity remaining, prompting the purchase. Graham Keogh called it “a winner,” citing performance, reliability and operational savings beyond expectations.
items.title: Wickham Freight Lines takes delivery of Australia’s first solar-powered electric reefer

items.summary: The United Nations says it is now inevitable that the world will miss its Paris Agreement goals due to decades of insufficient climate action, projecting warming could reach 2.6 and then 2.8 degrees Celsius by century's end. A new UNEP report titled The Point of Return argues leaders can still limit peak warming and shorten overshoot. The article notes this comes amid the fastest clean energy buildout in history: renewables now exceed coal share, one in four cars sold last year was electric, avoiding 1.2 million barrels of oil a day. Yet Politico warns emissions rose as methane stayed flat, and rising demand from AI and development may make efficiency gains essential. As quoted by David Frykman, wind and solar cannot be embargoed or blockaded.
items.title: UN Report Warns of Overshoot Despite Clean Energy Surge

items.summary: Turkey, host of COP31 in Antalya from 9th–20th November under a joint presidency with Australia, is urging wealthy nations to spend more on climate support than defence. COP31 president-designate Murat Kurum argued that climate change itself is the security issue and NATO members should exceed their planned 5% GDP increase for defence by 2035, citing lower pre-disaster costs versus post-disaster spending of up to 10 units per one unit spent beforehand. Australia’s minister Chris Bowen noted only 0.2% of climate finance reaches small island developing countries. Both hosts also face criticism over expanding fossil fuel projects amid a global goal of 35% electricity by 2035, currently around 21%.
items.title: COP31 Host Pushes NATO Nations Toward Climate Spending Over Defence

items.summary: An author argues that the Trump administration's FY2027 Department of Energy budget request cuts useful energy research alongside weak technological bets. Across thirteen selected DOE technology program lines, FY2026 enacted funding totaled about $4.288 billion; the FY2027 request reduces it to $2.618 billion, a decline of roughly 39%. Solar, wind, vehicles and buildings fall from $1.005 billion to only $40 million, about a 96% reduction. The author contends that early-stage research should answer credible questions, demonstrations resolve specific uncertainties, and deployment accelerates viable technologies, warning that hollowing out government evaluation weakens both sides of the process.
items.title: CleanTechnica Criticizes Trump DOE Budget Cuts on Clean Energy Research

items.summary: The Guardian argues that London mayor Sadiq Khan's long-running plan to close the busiest stretch of Oxford Street to traffic will finally proceed, framing it as a test case for greener cities. The Greater London Authority hopes the scheme will help a high street whose vacant shops have more than quadrupled since the pandemic and estimates £82m annual value from increased footfall, though this remains unproven here even if research elsewhere supports pedestrianisation boosting sales.
items.title: Guardian editorial backs Oxford Street pedestrianisation as people-first model

items.summary: Four UK collecting-society chief executives argue that AI firms and device manufacturers should pay the creators whose work they use. They point to a proposed Smart Fund that could raise up to £300m a year, noting that visual artists earn a median of just £12,500 annually — 47% lower in real terms than in 2010.
items.title: UK creators' societies call for government action on creator payments

items.summary: Former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Ghulam Nabi Azad criticised National Conference president Farooq Abdullah over his remarks on Pakistan's role in Kashmir, calling the statement completely incorrect. Azad asserted that Pakistan was an enemy of India and its people. He wrote on X: 'If anyone is an enemy of India and the people of J&K, it is Pakistan.' The exchange reflects ongoing political tension between the two leaders.
items.title: Azad Calls Pakistan Enemy of India and Kashmiris, Rebuts Farooq Abdullah

items.summary: Sections of indigenous communities in Arunachal Pradesh oppose the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), citing concerns about displacement, environmental impact, and livelihoods. Protests turned violent in Pasighat on Friday. The project is viewed as a strategic response to China's hydropower development upstream, but local Adi community members fear the dam could submerge ancestral land, displace villages, and permanently alter the Siang River ecosystem.
items.title: Arunachal locals protest India's Siang dam over displacement fears

items.summary: Jiang Feng, a CGTN special commentator, argues that China-EU relations are being reshaped by intensifying geopolitical competition and strained multilateralism. Writing for the outlet's opinion section, he notes that both sides recently gathered in Paris at the eighth Friends of the Paris Agreement High-Level Dialogue to explore climate challenges. He observes that while their regulatory approaches differ—Europe favoring standards-setting and China prioritizing development—their complementary strengths could support joint rulemaking and technological collaboration. Framing these differences as opportunities rather than confrontation, he calls for strengthened consultation mechanisms and shared green transition efforts.
items.title: China and Europe urged to deepen climate cooperation amid global tensions

items.summary: Two CGTN special commentators argue that a party's governing vitality depends on how its development benefits ordinary citizens rather than numerical growth. Writing ahead of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, which convenes in Beijing from October 26 to 29, Gao Lei and Wen Jiaqi contend that misjudging governance performance pushes officials toward vanity projects at public expense. They say correcting this requires optimizing how officials are evaluated, shifting emphasis toward livelihoods, environment protection, innovation and safety. The authors note the Party's anti-corruption drive reinforces people-centered power use and present these views as commentary reflecting their own opinions rather than official CGTN positions.
items.title: CGTN Commentators Frame People's Well-being as China's True Governance Measure

items.summary: María Corina Machado, aged 59 and Nobel peace prize winner, announced her return to Venezuela almost a year after leaving for the award. Her ally Edmundo González confirmed it via social media posts on Sunday. Footage placed her in Barquisimeto, about 220 miles west of Caracas, at the Sanctuary of the Divine Shepherdess. The Trump administration reportedly opposed the move amid its ties to interim president Delcy Rodríguez and seized Nicolás Maduro.
items.title: Exiled Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returns home

items.summary: Serbia votes as Aleksandar Vučić faces a grassroots challenge from the leaderless Student List, whose victory is uncertain amid conflicting pre-election polls and low turnout projections. The night may be contested by recounts or irregularity claims, with observers monitoring closely.
items.title: Serbia's Student List challenges Vučić in close election

items.summary: This Euronews news bulletin, dated October 25th, 2026 – Evening, offers a round-up of the most important stories from around Europe and beyond. The newsroom presents latest and breaking news across world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel, framed as an independent overview with a European perspective intended to help viewers make sense of a fast-moving day.
items.title: Latest news bulletin | October 25th, 2026 – Evening

items.summary: Two storms, Austen and Boelo, disrupted transport across northern Europe over the weekend, causing temporary power cuts to more than 150,000 homes. Winds of up to 135 kilometres an hour were recorded in Argyll and Bute, Scotland, while fallen trees blocked roads and rail lines. Hundreds of flights were cancelled or diverted, including at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport. In Britain some 82,000 homes lost power; France saw nearly 60,000 affected, with at least 10,000 in Germany. The Met Office warned Storm Boelo posed a danger to life from flying debris and crashing waves.
items.title: Storms Austen and Boelo cut power across northern Europe

items.summary: About 1,250 sheep and 160 goats began the annual Transhumance Festival in Madrid from Casa de Campo, crossing Puente del Rey into the historic centre. Residents watched as folk musicians played and shepherds led the animals through streets usually reserved for traffic. The event celebrates transhumance, moving livestock between summer and winter pastures along traditional drovers' routes.
items.title: Thousands of Sheep March Through Madrid for Transhumance Festival

items.summary: María Corina Machado, anti-Chavista opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate, returned to Venezuela after nearly 10 months abroad. She posted on social media that she was back; former presidential candidate Edmundo González Urrutia confirmed it. Over the past three months she made at least seven attempts by boat, flight and overland routes from Virginia, Panama and Curaçao, each blocked or canceled, with little doubt her passage depended on United States approval that never came. She aims to rejoin opposition politics ahead of an uncertain electoral process. Although a poll gives her 57.4% support as of August per AtlasIntel’s Latam Pulse for Bloomberg, she has limited influence over current decisions. The Rodríguez government denies opposing the return but warns she will answer for past actions, including claims that she promoted a U.S. invasion.
items.title: Opposition Leader María Corina Machado Returns to Venezuela

items.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned home after over 10 months in exile, writing on X that she was back with her supporters. Her ally Edmundo González confirmed the return and said it would guide Venezuela toward freedom. Machado had won a 2023 primary election with more than 90% of the vote but was barred from office by Maduro's government.
items.title: Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile

items.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres met Arab League Secretary-General Nabil Fahmy in Cairo on Sunday to discuss regional developments and promote peace through dialogue. The UN office said talks also covered cooperation between the organizations for stability across the Arab region, plus support for people affected by crises in Gaza and Sudan. Guterres arrived as part of consultations aimed at de-escalating tensions involving Iran.
items.title: UN chief meets Arab League leader in Egypt over regional de-escalation

items.summary: María Corina Machado, Venezuela's opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate, returned to the country after ten months abroad. She announced her arrival on X with a post declaring 'I'm here, with you all.' Her first public appearance was at the Church of Santa Rosa in Lara State, where she faced an ecstatic crowd. Edmundo González Urrutia confirmed the return.
items.title: Venezuela Opposition Leader María Corina Machado Returns After Exile

items.summary: On Sunday, Liverpool beat Brighton & Hove Albion 2-0 to record their first Premier League home win of the season. Meanwhile, Manchester United lost 3-0 away to Bournemouth in an embarrassing result that increased pressure on manager Michael Carrick, who had benched captain Bruno Fernandes after criticism following a Champions League loss.
items.title: Liverpool win at home as Manchester United suffer defeat under Carrick

items.summary: A translated German article examines whether protein shakes and bars suit adolescents, noting that a University of Michigan survey in 2024 found just under half of parents said their children aged 13 to 17 consumed such products. The piece cites Statista on an estimated 25% rise in Germany's fitness protein market between March 2024 and March 2025, then turns to the German Nutrition Society (DGE) recommendations for intake levels by age group. It lists concerns — added sugar, possible doping substances found by Cologne researchers, acne risk, and reduced normal meals — before concluding that supplements are unnecessary for most athletes but may help those with allergies or low appetite.
items.title: German guide weighs protein supplements for teenagers

items.summary: Early reports indicate a record high turnout as Serbian voters cast ballots in parliamentary elections, with 46% having voted by 14:00 local time (13:00 GMT), nearly a million more than December 2023. The surge fuels opposition hopes that the Student List can oust Aleksandar Vučić and his SNS party, who have governed since 2012. Most commentators suggest a final turnout of 65% or above would favour students. Tensions are high across Serbia as police close streets around the Republic Electoral Commission amid fears of fraud by SNS loyalists. Voting ends at 20:00, with results expected two hours later.
items.title: Serbian Voters Turn Out in Record Numbers Amid Student Uprising

items.summary: As Israel prepares for elections described as pivotal in its history, voters confront whether to reelect Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or back challenger Gadi Eisenkot. Many Israelis say they are both defiant and weary after three years of war that began with the Oct. 7 Hamas attack, which killed nearly 1,200 people and took 251 hostages. Polls show most voters were not troubled by Gaza suffering and believe there are no innocent civilians there. Eisenkot promises a national investigation into the security failure and restraint in the West Bank, while Netanyahu campaigns on his wars as proof Israel is safer. The race remains tight, with polls showing neither candidate has a clear path to victory.
items.title: Israelis weigh voting out Netanyahu amid war's toll

items.summary: Gabon's media regulator, the High Communication Authority (HAC), said social media access was restored on Saturday after an eight-month suspension. The HAC had blamed online content for stoking conflict and framed the ban as a step to better regulate platforms and improve content moderation with Meta, TikTok and YouTube. Users must now provide formal identification, ending online anonymity.
items.title: Gabon Restores Social Media After Eight-Month Ban Amid Unrest

items.summary: The Amaury Sport Organisation said on Sunday that the 2027 Dakar Rally would not be held in Saudi Arabia, citing security concerns amid attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis. The event, scheduled from 1 to 15 January 2027 and run there since 2020, would move to a location announced later; organisers called the decision exceptional and one-off, with the landmark 50th edition planned for Saudi Arabia in 2028.
items.title: Dakar Rally organisers cancel Saudi Arabia edition for 2027

items.summary: President Donald Trump labelled former President Barack Obama “grossly incompetent” in a social media post, one day after Obama attacked the incumbent during Democratic rallies in Ohio and Michigan. Obama blamed the Trump administration for rising living costs and an unnecessary war with Iran while campaigning for Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed. Nationally, polls suggest Democrats could regain control of the House but face tougher competition in the Senate.
items.title: Trump Calls Obama Incompetent After Ohio and Michigan Rallies

items.summary: An opinion writer calls it a tragedy that Israel hosts two charismatic populists, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and national security minister Itamar Ben Gvir. The author argues the damage their coalition has caused since taking power in 2022 could deepen if they win re-election this week. Describing another Netanyahu victory as inconceivable, he notes both men led Israel's security on Oct. 7, 2023, when Hamas launched a massed attack.
items.title: A columnist weighs whether Israel can survive a populist government alone

items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition announced Sunday that it intercepted and destroyed 10 ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi group from Yemen toward southern Saudi Arabia. Spokesman Turki al-Maliki confirmed the shots on X, giving no details about injuries or damage. The interceptions followed an earlier report of a downed cruise missile near Khamis Mushait and came amid escalating attacks on Saudi aviation and energy infrastructure since 2015.
items.title: Saudi-led Coalition Reports Intercepting Ten Houthi Ballistic Missiles

items.summary: On Sunday, opposition party officials demanded that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi personally explain her government’s consumption tax cut legislation in parliament. During a televised debate, they questioned the lack of details about a planned benefit program and the uncertain economic impact of cutting the food tax rate to 1% for two years. Yasuhiro Nakagawa of Komeito called it unprecedented that a bill establishing a new system lacked specific figures.
items.title: Opposition parties demand Takaichi explain tax cut bill

items.summary: Whale remains found off a Perth beach prompted authorities to warn of possible shark activity in Sorrento after removing the carcass tail. This is the second whale carcass this week and third in a month, raising concerns as beaches grow crowded before summer. The area had closed about five weeks ago following Greg O'Neill's fatal great white shark attack.
items.title: Perth Beaches Close After More Whale Remains Found Near Sorrento

items.summary: The article profiles Peter Thiel, a 58-year-old Silicon Valley figure described as the most influential since Steve Jobs' emergence in the late 1970s. It traces his funding of Hulk Hogan's lawyers in their $140 million Gawker victory, which he saw as signaling social change and later backed with a speech at the Republican National Convention that helped launch Donald Trump's career. Thiel is characterized as a libertarian promoter of technoconservatism behind figures like J.D. Vance and Ted Cruz, who opposes international organizations such as the United Nations and NATO. In late September he warned about the 'Antichrist' and AI regulation in Nashville. Critics including Gil Durán call him the father of an extremist sect that cloaks anti-democratic ideas in religious rhetoric, while philosopher Mark Coeckelbergh notes his belief in elite-led authoritarian governance.
items.title: Peter Thiel's Antichrist Theology and Political Influence

items.summary: This article examines how Mozambique's communities of Indian origin navigate questions of identity, belonging, and legal status. It explains that the term monhé is used as an identity marker but is not a legal category, distinguishing between origin, nationality, and citizenship. The piece traces the history of these populations through trade networks predating 1975 independence, colonial-era nationality rules under Portuguese rule, and post-independence laws defining who qualified for Mozambican nationality. It notes that decolonization produced cases of statelessness while others became full citizens, concluding that belonging often spans both African and Asian heritage.
items.title: Mozambique's Indian-origin community and its contested nationality

items.summary: The India-US interim trade pact remains stalled despite US optimism that it is nearly complete, sources said. Washington insists on retaining an 18 per cent tariff rate or lowering proposed tariffs to around 14 per cent or 12 per cent, while New Delhi refuses anything above the current 10 per cent levy under Section 301. India also weighs domestic political risks of agricultural concessions ahead of US mid-term elections and seeks assurances before deciding how to proceed, a source tracking the matter told businessline.
items.title: India-US Trade Pact Stalls Over Tariff Dispute

items.summary: Delhi Police registered an FIR against opposition MPs for alleged trespassing at Jamia Millia Islamia University, following a complaint by university authorities amid student protests demanding the restoration of the Students' Union. Jamia Registrar Md Mahtab Alam Rizvi accused Congress MPs Imran Masood and Imran Pratapgarhi of entering without authorisation, with one reportedly breaking a lock. The protest began on October 12; last union elections were held in 2005, before dissolution in 2006.
items.title: Delhi Police Register FIR Against Opposition MPs Over Jamia Trespass

items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir Congress distanced itself from National Conference president Farooq Abdullah's remark that Pakistan was helping Kashmiris by keeping the Kashmir issue alive at international fora. Chief spokesperson Ravinder Sharma said via a post on X that Pakistan has no right to interfere in India's internal affairs, since J&K is an integral part of India. Speaking separately, Sharma suggested Abdullah's remarks reflected frustration over the Centre's failure to restore statehood and urged him to clarify his intent. Kashmiri Pandit groups Panun Kashmir and the Jammu State People's Movement lodged a police complaint seeking an FIR against Abdullah at the Channi police station in Jammu under Sections 152, 196 and 197 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). BJP leader Jahanzaib Sirwal also criticised Abdullah for relying on Pakistan to question India's intentions. The remarks were delivered Saturday at a party event in Baramulla.
items.title: Congress distances itself from Farooq Abdullah's Kashmir remarks amid FIR complaint

items.summary: Neil Armstrong's childhood home in Wapakoneta, Ohio has been acquired by the Auglaize County Historical Society after retired pilot Ken Schreiber donated $400,000. The sale was finalised on Monday following a 2019 report that no one had come forward to preserve it. Restoration of the two-storey house is planned for its appearance during Armstrong's childhood years, with public tours targeted by 2030 for the astronaut's birth anniversary. Gerald Siesel, the society's president, said fundraising and maintenance remain needed before visitors can be welcomed.
items.title: Retired pilot's donation preserves Neil Armstrong childhood home in Ohio

items.summary: Brazilian voters head to a closely contested runoff between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. Polls show a neck-and-neck race that could shape Latin America's largest economy and its ties with the United States. The campaign centers on rising living costs, crime, corruption and public finances, alongside foreign policy after Washington's 2025 tariffs.
items.title: Lula vs Flavio Bolsonaro: 5 key issues shaping Brazil’s neck-and-neck election

items.summary: Delhi Police reportedly filed an FIR against Congress MPs Imran Masood and Imran Pratapgarhi for trespassing on the campus of Delhi's Jamia Millia Islamia university, where a protest over student-union restoration has continued since October 12. The FIR followed a complaint by JMI accusing them of inciting unrest amid hunger strikes. University classes shifted online from Saturday until further notice; protesting students questioned the move and said their concerns go unheard. Student Mohammad Ayan Khan blamed corruption for the union demand, alleging hostel seats are handed out for profit while complaints against professors receive no action. The university set up a committee to draft the JMISU constitution after its last elections in 2006.
items.title: Delhi Police File Trespass FIR Against Two Congress MPs Amid Jamia Protest

items.summary: Police said on Sunday that a Special Investigation Team registered an eighth case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 against R Veeramani, chairman of Gem Group of Companies. The SIT booked him on October 21, 2026 after receiving a complaint about a victim who was a minor at the time. Eight persons have been arrested in total, and police said action has been taken based on complaints concerning 12 affected minor girls so far.
items.title: Industrialist R Veeramani Booked in Eighth POCSO Case, Police Say

items.summary: BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao attacked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday, calling him one of the biggest liars and promise-makers in Indian politics for failing to fulfil election pledges while avoiding visits to Telangana. He alleged that before the 2023 elections Rahul made 420 promises, including implementing six guarantees within 100 days and delivering all 420 promises—more than 1,000 days later—and accused the Revanth Reddy-led Congress government of turning the state into an ATM for him. Rama Rao said more than 1,000 days have passed since those pledges were made.
items.title: KTR Accuses Rahul Gandhi of Breaking Telangana Election Promises

items.summary: An editorial argues that concerns over the System for Identification and Registration (SIR) exclusions and software transparency warrant restoring voting rights before the 2027 Assembly polls. It claims election credibility has been damaged by manipulative processes, especially in West Bengal, and notes roughly 130 million voters were removed from rolls. Assuming about 20 million may have died since last update, around 110 million remain excluded from an eligible one billion. The piece calls for the Election Commission of India to act on restoring disenfranchised nationals' rights.
items.title: Activists Urge India to Restore Voting Rights Before 2027 Polls

items.summary: Sam Acho’s family began providing free medical care in Nigeria in 1989 through annual missions run by Living Hope Christian Ministries, founded by his father Dr. Sonny Acho and carried on with his mother Christie Acho. The short visits treated thousands of patients but could not offer lasting support. Acho’s two Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award nominations in 2016 and 2017 each brought a $50,000 charitable donation, totaling $100,000 that he directed to Living Hope Christian Ministries for hospital construction. Part of a wider fundraising effort, the money helped fund the project, which opened as the Living Hope Medical Center in June 2017 after years of work since 1989.
items.title: Sam Acho’s NFL Awards Fund Nigeria Hospital

items.summary: A political dispute erupted after Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge made remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi during an event in Patna, prompting condemnation from Union Home Minister Amit Shah and other Bharatiya Janata Party leaders. A formal police complaint was lodged at the Kotwali Police Station by BJP State Working Committee member Krishna Singh Kallu. The Congress defended Kharge as using colloquial political slang while accusing BJP of past insults.
items.title: Congress President Kharge Faces BJP Demands for Apology Over Modi Remarks

items.summary: Delhi Police registered an FIR against three Members of Parliament following a complaint by the Jamia Millia Islamia administration alleging they jumped over the university gate wall to enter without permission and attempted to disrupt the atmosphere. The action comes amid ongoing student protests concerning student union elections, with demonstrating students detained and online classes shifted for several days.
items.title: Jamia Row: Delhi Police File FIR Against 3 MPs For Trespassing; Students Detained Amid Protests

items.summary: India beat Zimbabwe by 121 runs in Vadodara on Sunday, sealing the three-match women's ODI series 2-0 with a game to spare. Left-arm spinner Vaishnavi Sharma took her maiden international four-wicket haul of 4-39 from 10 overs, while Deepti Sharma added 3-32 after an unbeaten century. Zimbabwe were bowled out for 207 in 48.5 overs off a target of 329 set by Harmanpreet Kaur (126) and Deepti (106 not out).
items.title: Sharma Sisters Seal India's Series Win Over Zimbabwe

items.summary: District Congress president Swatantra Joshi claimed the Special Intensive Revision removed 1,01,836 names from electoral rolls in Madhya Pradesh's Dhar district. He cited a fall across seven Assembly constituencies and statewide declines of about 5.74 crore to 5.39 crore voters. National spokesperson Charanjit Singh Sapra demanded the commissioner resign and accused the BJP of interfering with voter lists, announcing rallies on Nov 1.
items.title: Congress Accuses Election Commission of Deleting Voters in MP's Dhar District

items.summary:
Netflix reported that customers are opening the app on fewer days and watching less, measured by its qualified play days metric. The decline began after a 2022 password-sharing crackdown and has continued, raising concerns about service value amid slowing revenue growth and slipping shares of US TV viewing. Leadership changes were made to address the softness in content strategy. Netflix maintains that churn remains steady at 2% and price increases have not caused abnormal cancellations, though advertising sales are projected to fall short by $300 million this year.

visual
items.title: Netflix Usage Declines as Leadership Changes Aim to Regain Growth

items.summary: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced at the NDTV World Summit in Delhi on October 23, 2026, that India could field its own smartphone brand—designed, manufactured and branded domestically by October 2028. He cited a prior PCB design challenge won over roughly three-and-a-half years as groundwork, while noting he did not reveal the brand name, price or launch date. The target remains an ambition amid challenges from Apple and Samsung.
items.title: India's IT Minister Sets October 2028 Goal for Homegrown Smartphone Brand

items.summary: Canadian municipal elections this fall include rat control as a platform issue, with several parties pledging action against city rat problems. Authors Christine Yanagawa and Kaylee Byers argue rats reflect broader concerns about housing, public services and civic engagement. Drawing on studies from high-income cities using synthesis and complex systems mapping methods, they examine social and environmental conditions linked to urban rats across neighbourhoods in Vancouver's upcoming election. They note that unhoused populations may face higher rat contact; in Vancouver the number of unhoused people increased 12 per cent between 2023 and 2025. The authors point to municipal bylaws, sanitation services like 311 and existing Healthy City Strategies as avenues for addressing root causes.
items.title: Rats on Canada's municipal ballots signal deeper urban issues

items.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia faculty and staff, along with the university's Vice-Chancellor and Registrar, convened a Saturday meeting to discuss next steps in an ongoing student protest. The demonstration began on October 12 after Delhi Police attempted to remove protesters from campus grounds. Students demand restoration of the suspended Jamia Millia Islamia Students' Union (JMISU), revocation of disciplinary action against them, and removal of the university's Chief Proctor.
items.title: Faculty convene meeting amid Jamia student agitation over suspended union

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, on October 25, 2026. He said a secure banking system needs digital infrastructure supported by robust data centres and powerful computing systems. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stressed resilient infrastructure for financial stability. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra emphasised leveraging emerging technologies to reach India’s goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047, training staff in AI, big data analytics, quantum and blockchain. The event was covered by Doordarshan on the same date.,
items.title: Modi Inaugurates RBI Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi warned that cyberattacks on banking could threaten economic security while inaugurating the RBI's new data centre in Odisha. He said modern warfare now targets economies, urging protection from 'cyber looters and cyber terrorists.' Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman noted the facility will host RTGS and NEFT systems.
items.title: Modi Warns Cyberattacks Threaten India's Banking System as Economy Grows

items.summary: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray said he deleted a documentary alleging long-standing ties between Gautam Adani and Narendra Modi, following a request conveyed through the Mumbai Police commissioner. Made by Sabeer Bhatia, it had been viewed more than 48 lakh times on X alone. Thackeray framed his opposition as being against monopoly rather than any individual.
items.title: Raj Thackeray Deletes Adani-Modi Documentary After Police Request

items.summary: BJP leaders accused Congress of ideological bankruptcy after Mallikarjun Kharge’s remark in Patna on October 25. Union Home Minister Amit Shah and BJP chief Nitin Nabin condemned the language as indecent, likening it to hooligans and a mafia gang. Kharge responded that even Modi's father would have to go, framing his words as defensible.
items.title: BJP Slams Kharge Over ‘Modi Ka Baap Bhi Jayega’ Remark

items.summary: Rishikesh Palve of Anand Rathi Wealth explains that mutual fund houses recently paused fresh investments in gold funds, affecting SIPs, switch-ins and lump-sum purchases. He notes the move follows higher gold imports, a stronger dollar and rupee depreciation. Existing investors can still redeem holdings while ETFs remain available, though demand may push their prices up. Palve advises treating gold as debt replacement rather than equity, keeping an 80% equity allocation intact, holding around 5–10% in gold and avoiding recency bias when chasing rising prices.
items.title: Anand Rathi Wealth Explains Gold ETFs and FoFs Amid Investment Restrictions

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department forecasts a depression over the Bay of Bengal to intensify into Cyclone Arnab, expected to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast around forenoon Wednesday, October 28. The system is projected to become a very severe cyclonic storm with sustained winds of 115-125 kmph and gusts reaching 140 kmph. Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry are also preparing for heavy rainfall, strong winds and possible flooding. Authorities in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have stepped up disaster preparedness, hoisted cyclone warning signals at nine ports and issued red warnings across five Odisha districts.
items.title: Cyclone Arnab Looms Over Andhra Pradesh Coast on October 28

items.summary: Indian equity mutual funds lost up to 9% last week, with international funds the biggest laggards. Mirae Asset NYSE FANG+ETF FoF posted around 9.06%, followed by Motilal Oswal Nasdaq 100 FOF at 7.45%. The top six of nearly 628 funds lost over 6.50%.
items.title: Equity funds fell sharply as international schemes led weekly losses

items.summary: A viral social media video claiming looted luxury goods were being sold in France during September–October 2026 protests was fact-checked as false. Using Google Lens reverse image search, the outlet traced it to a Madrid post on X dated October 6, 2026, showing street vendors near Gran Via. The claim is debunked.
items.title: Fact Check Debunks Viral France Loot Video
